newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to cut taxes by 75 bln Ffr over 5 years.
newsitem.headline: France to cut taxes by 75 bln Ffr over 5 years.

text.p: The French government plans to cut income taxes by 75 billion francs over the next five years, the government said in a statement on Thursday.
It said that it would cut income taxes by 25 billion francs on income earned in 1996 and payable in 1997.
But given additional taxation of seven billion francs to fund the welfare system, the net tax cut next year would be 18 billion francs, the government said.
It said it was cutting all income tax rates next year, bringing the top rate of tax to 54 percent from 56.8 percent. The bottom rate of tax will be lowered to 10.5 percent next year from 12 percent.
Over the course of its five-year tax reforms, the government said it would reduce the top rate of tax to 47 percent and the lowest rate of tax to seven percent.
